watchlistGrid.columnCountAt380:
2 columns — arithmetic:

Container chain at a 380px viewport:
- body/html have no horizontal padding (apps/web/src/app/globals.css:12-25; box-sizing: border-box globally at :6-10).
- AppShell .main at <=767.98px (/Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/shell/AppShell.module.css:118-123):
    padding-left:  calc(var(--space-md) + env(safe-area-inset-left, 0))  = 16px + 0 = 16px
    padding-right: calc(var(--space-md) + env(safe-area-inset-right, 0)) = 16px + 0 = 16px
  (--space-md: 16px — apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css:168; safe-area insets are 0 on a non-notched 380px browser viewport)
- .main content box = 380 - 16 - 16 = 348px
- watchlist .page is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` with no padding (page.module.css:2-6), so .grid's content box = 348px.

auto-fill with minmax(132px, 1fr) and gap: var(--space-md) = 16px:
  n tracks fit iff  n*132 + (n-1)*16 <= 348
  n = 2 -> 264 + 16 = 280 <= 348  OK
  n = 3 -> 396 + 32 = 428 >  348  fails
  => n = 2
Equivalent closed form: floor((348 + 16) / (132 + 16)) = floor(364 / 148) = floor(2.459) = 2.
Resulting track width = (348 - 16) / 2 = 166px per column.

CONTRAST — Browse at the same 380px viewport (the LD-14 defect):
  computeColumns(348, 168, 16) = floor((348 + 16) / (168 + 16)) = floor(364 / 184) = floor(1.978) = 1
  -> ONE 348px-wide poster ("jumbo single poster"). The .skeletonGrid CSS agrees: 1*168 <= 348 but 2*168 + 16 = 352 > 348, so auto-fill also yields 1 track, stretched to 348px by 1fr.
Note: on a desktop browser narrowed to 380px WITH a classic (non-overlay) scrollbar, subtract ~15px from 348 -> 333px; Watchlist still yields 2 columns (2*132 + 16 = 280 <= 333), Browse still yields 1.

cssArchitecture:
Plain CSS Modules + a small set of globally-imported CSS files. No Tailwind (no tailwind.config anywhere; no tailwind dependency in apps/web/package.json), no CSS-in-JS, no styled-components, no shared style package (grep for `minmax` / `gridTemplateColumns` across all .ts/.tsx in apps/web/src returns ZERO hits — every grid lives in CSS; and `find packages -name "*.css"` returns nothing, so no workspace package ships styles apps/web could import).

GLOBAL LAYER — /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/app/globals.css is imported once by the root layout (/Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx:6 `import "./globals.css";`). Its first three lines are the entire global-stylesheet manifest:
  globals.css:2  @import "../styles/tokens.css";
  globals.css:3  @import "../styles/fonts.css";
  globals.css:4  @import "../styles/glass.css";
globals.css itself then holds the reset (box-sizing, body, headings overflow-wrap, focus rings/keyframes, prefers-reduced-motion) and two globally-scoped class families (.nf-* for the root not-found boundary, with the reason they live here documented at :116-128).

DESIGN TOKENS — /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css is the single source of truth (its own header says so, :3-28). All tokens are CSS custom properties on bare `:root` (:30-328), plus three `:root[data-accent="..."]` override blocks (:338-348) and one `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) :root` block (:350-358). Dark-only; the light-theme block was deliberately removed.
Token categories and the px-valued ones (relevant to LD-19 sizing):
  --radius-*        :34-38   (pill/lg/md/sm/full)
  --motion-* / --ease-*   :41-45
  --color-* / --fill-*    :48-160
  --space-3xs..3xl  :164-172  (2/4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64px)  <- --space-md: 16px is the gap on BOTH grids
  --font-* / --wdth-* / --text-* / --mono-* / --track-* / --leading-* / --weight-*  :175-207
  --shadow-*        :213-219
  --chrome-*        :224-226
  --sidebar-bg      :237
  --mobile-tabbar-height / --mobile-header-height / --mobile-header-height-back  :254-256  <- the existing precedent for a NON-color, NON-space, px LAYOUT token; each carries an inline comment justifying its value
  --scanlines / --vignette / --brand-* / --color-bg-splash / --scanlines-splash  :278-318
  semantic aliases --bg/--surface/--overlay/--text/--muted/--border/--focus  :321-327
NAMING CONVENTION: lowercase kebab, `--<category>-<variant>[-<modifier>]`, category first (--space-2xs, --color-text-muted, --mobile-header-height-back, --radius-lg). Every non-obvious token carries an inline `/* ... */` explaining its value and its consumers. There are currently ZERO `--grid-*` custom properties (`grep -rn -- "--grid-" apps/web/src` returns nothing) and zero sizing tokens for grid minimums.

COMPONENT LAYER — one co-located `*.module.css` per component/route (`apps/web/src/app/<route>/page.module.css`, `apps/web/src/components/<area>/<Component>.module.css`). Modules never re-declare literals that tokens.css owns; border-radius literals are actively banned by stylelint (see below).

CROSS-MODULE REUSE — CSS Modules `composes:`, in two forms, 30 call sites total:
  (a) `composes: <class> from global;` — pulls a class out of a globals-imported stylesheet. THE ONLY existing example is `.glass` (defined at /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/styles/glass.css:21-25, consumed at app/setup/page.module.css:26, app/styleguide/page.module.css:120, components/music/MiniPlayerBar.module.css:14, components/music/QueueDrawer.module.css:3, components/shell/MobileHeader.module.css:10, components/shell/MobileTabBar.module.css:11, components/detail/AmbientHero.module.css:67, components/detail/SceneBanner.module.css:83, components/player/Scrubber.module.css:95, components/player/UnavailableScreen.module.css:12). glass.css's own header (:12-14) documents the pattern and the deliberate rule that the recipe sets only its own properties and never border-radius/box-shadow so it cannot fight a consumer's cascade.
  (b) `composes: <class> from "<relative path to another module>";` — e.g. `composes: button secondary from "../ui/Button.module.css"` (app/browse/page.module.css:60, app/watchlist/page.module.css:46, app/people/[id]/page.module.css:59, components/detail/PlayLink.module.css:3, WatchlistToggle.module.css:7, SeriesDetailScreen.module.css:62,:97), `composes: track|segment from "../ui/SegmentedControl.module.css"` (LibraryPills:8,:13, SortControl:3,:7, SeasonPillTabs:17,:21, ZoneControls:20,:24,:28), `composes: dialog from "./Overlay.module.css"` (SheetOrModal:10).

STYLELINT — a single flat config at /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/.stylelintrc.json (29 lines; the only other copies on disk are gitignored installer stage artifacts). `extends: ["stylelint-config-standard"]`, no plugins beyond stylelint + stylelint-config-standard (apps/web/package.json devDependencies). Run via apps/web `"lint": "eslint src --max-warnings=0 && stylelint \"src/**/*.css\""`, reached from the root `pnpm gate`'s lint step (`turbo run lint`).
THE PRECEDENT LD-19's new rule should follow is already in this file at :15-27 — `declaration-property-value-allowed-list` keyed by a property regex, used to make every hand-written border-radius literal a lint failure:
  "declaration-property-value-allowed-list": {
    "/^border-radius$/": [ "/^var\\(--radius-(pill|lg|md|sm|full)\\)$/", ... , "0", "inherit" ],
    "/^border-(top|bottom)-(left|right)-radius$/": [ ... ]
  }
Two mechanical notes for the LD-19 rule: (i) the config is FLAT — exempting the utility's own file (styles/grid.css) requires adding a stylelint `overrides` block, which this config does not have yet; (ii) a naive `/minmax\(/` disallow-list on grid-template-columns would also fire on the five legitimate `minmax(0, Nfr)` min-content-suppression sites (AlbumDetailScreen:82,:88, MovieDetailScreen:109, system-cards:54) and on MovieDetailScreen:102 — the pattern must exempt `minmax(0,` and the lane must decide MovieDetailScreen:102's fate.

CSS-SOURCE-READING TESTS — this repo already pins CSS rules by reading stylesheet TEXT in vitest (jsdom never evaluates imported CSS). The general-sweep precedent is /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/ld14-mono-scale-conformance.test.ts (walks every *.module.css, parses rule blocks, asserts a design rule); narrower ones include components/admin/settings/phosphor-mobile-css.test.ts, components/ui/BlazeSpinner.purge.test.ts, components/shell/Sidebar.blaze-purge.test.ts and lib/home-rail-geometry.test.ts (which reads AppShell.module.css's max-width). Each carries an inline comment giving the measured basis for the number. NOT a token file but THE utility-class precedent: a globals-imported stylesheet defining one recipe class (.glass at :21-25) consumed by 10 modules via `composes: glass from global;`. Its header (:12-14) states the pattern and the discipline ("this recipe still deliberately does NOT set border-radius or box-shadow, so it never fights a component's own declarations in the cascade"). The global-stylesheet manifest: @import "../styles/tokens.css"; @import "../styles/fonts.css"; @import "../styles/glass.css". A new styles/grid.css must be added here (a 4th @import) or its class will not exist for `composes: ... from global`.

sharedComponents.detail: THE BIGGEST LEAK VECTOR — but it leaks toward the RESTRICTED ZONE, not toward Watchlist. VirtualPosterGrid is imported by app/browse/page.tsx:32 AND by components/restricted/ZoneBrowseGrid.tsx:23 (used at :61). ZoneBrowseGrid is the shared card renderer behind /restricted/browse, /restricted/performers/[id] (filmography) and /restricted/studios/[id] (catalog) — its own header says so at :6-9. NEITHER app/browse/page.tsx (lines 232-241 and 244-271) NOR ZoneBrowseGrid.tsx (lines 61-86) passes `itemWidth` or `gap`, so all four surfaces run on DEFAULT_ITEM_WIDTH=168 / DEFAULT_GAP=16. Any LD-14 change made INSIDE VirtualPosterGrid.tsx (or its .module.css) silently reshapes the three restricted-zone poster walls too. To confine LD-14 to Browse, the change must be a prop passed from app/browse/page.tsx, or the component must gain an explicit opt-in — deciding which is a lane decision, not a discovery finding.

Same leak, CSS side: .skeletonGrid is the loading skeleton for all four surfaces above (VirtualPosterGrid.tsx:241 renders it in the `if (loading)` branch, which every caller reaches). Editing minmax(168px,1fr) here changes the restricted zone's skeletons as well. Also note components/restricted/RestrictedZoneEmptyState.tsx:9 explicitly cites this module's `.empty` class as its visual reference.

computeColumns is pure and has exactly one caller (VirtualPosterGrid.tsx:144) but is unit-tested in isolation (lib/grid-windowing.test.ts) and its contract is quoted in components/admin/VirtualList.tsx:7-9 (a separate single-column virtualizer that copies the model but does NOT import this function). Changing computeColumns's signature or its floor(…) semantics touches Browse + all three restricted-zone walls at once; adding a breakpoint-aware clamp is safer done in VirtualPosterGrid.tsx (or via a new prop) than inside this pure module.

Shared by BOTH pages: VirtualPosterGrid.tsx:38 imports it for the Browse skeleton cells (rendered at :244-245 with height={itemWidth * POSTER_ASPECT} = 252px and a 70%-width caption bar); app/watchlist/page.tsx:26 imports it for the Watchlist skeleton (rendered at :132 as `<Skeleton radius="md" height={252} />`). Both hardcode a 252px height that assumes a 168px-wide column — neither re-derives it from the actual track width. Any LD-14/LD-19 column-width change makes these skeletons the wrong aspect ratio unless they are updated in the same pass.

Shared data hook, NOT styling: app/watchlist/page.tsx:27 imports it out of the browse folder (`import { useCursorFeed, type CursorPage } from "../../components/browse/useCursorFeed.js"`). Listed only so a lane does not mistake the browse/ folder path for a styling coupling — there is none here.

The one CSS module both routes actually compose from: `composes: button secondary from "../../components/ui/Button.module.css"` (browse .retryButton, watchlist .loadMore). Not grid-related; a genuine shared surface if a lane touches button sizing.

NOT SHARED — deliberately duplicated. PosterCell.module.css's header (:3-9) states it is "deliberately not composed from components/home/PosterCard.module.css", and WatchlistPosterCard.module.css's header (:3-8) says it is the "Same recipe as components/browse/PosterCell.module.css" but a separate file. There is no `composes:` between them. Both define an identical `.tile { width: 100%; }` (PosterCell:11-19 / WatchlistPosterCard:9-17) and `.imageWrap { aspect-ratio: 2 / 3; }` (PosterCell:24 / WatchlistPosterCard:22), so BOTH cards take whatever width their grid track gives them. GOOD NEWS FOR LD-14: a Browse-side change to PosterCell.module.css cannot leak to Watchlist. BAD NEWS: the two files must be kept in sync by hand if a lane changes the tile recipe — there are three such near-clones (PosterCell, WatchlistPosterCard, and components/home/PosterCard.module.css), plus a fourth partial in components/restricted/ZonePosterCard.tsx (whose header at :10-21 documents the duplication).

THE WATCHLIST-SIDE LEAK VECTOR: WatchlistPosterCard is ALSO rendered by Home's "Your Watchlist" rail. Home sizes it with its own fixed-width wrapper — app/home/page.module.css:12-15 `.watchlistCell { width: 160px; flex-shrink: 0; }` inside a horizontal Row scroller. So any change to WatchlistPosterCard.module.css affects Home too; any change to app/watchlist/page.module.css's .grid/.cell does not.

The shared container both grids live inside — `.main` sets the content-box width every column count is computed from. Desktop: padding var(--space-xl) with padding-left calc(210px + var(--space-xl)) (:81-84, dropping to 76px at <=1279.98px, :108-110); mobile <=767.98px: padding-left/right calc(var(--space-md) + env(safe-area-inset-*)) (:119-122). Also `max-width: 1920px` and `overflow-x: hidden` (:85-86) — the overflow-x:hidden is why a too-wide grid clips silently instead of producing a scrollbar (MovieDetailScreen.module.css:93 cites exactly this). lib/home-rail-geometry.test.ts reads this file's max-width and fails if it drifts.

A THIRD poster layout that is neither of the two in scope and uses NO minmax at all — `.grid { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-md); }` with `.cell { width: 160px; }`. Its header (ChildPosterGrid.tsx:6-7) and WatchlistPosterCard.module.css:6-8 both cite the `.cell { width: 160px }` convention as the house pattern for sizing a poster card from its host. Flagged so a lane sweeping "all poster grids" does not miss it — but it is outside LD-19's minmax inventory by construction.

outOfScope: NAME COLLISION — 'LD-14' ALREADY MEANS SOMETHING ELSE IN THIS REPO. The existing LD-14 is the mono-scale contrast rule (subtle/hint text colors banned on the --mono-* scale), documented at apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css:81-92 and pinned by a whole test file, /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/components/ld14-mono-scale-conformance.test.ts (its header cites 'LD-14/AUD-A4v3-003'). It has nothing to do with grids. An implementation lane briefed on 'LD-14' will find that file first and be misled. Recommend the new decision be referenced by a distinct tag in code comments, or that the collision be called out explicitly in the lane brief.

BROWSE .page HEIGHT IS DESKTOP-ONLY MATH, UNGUARDED ON MOBILE. /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/apps/web/src/app/browse/page.module.css:6 `height: calc(100vh - 64px - (var(--space-xl) * 2));` with `min-height: 480px` at :7, and NO media-query override anywhere in the file. The 64px is the DESKTOP topbar height and --space-xl (32px) is the DESKTOP .main padding. Below 767.98px the real chrome is --mobile-header-height (112px) + --mobile-tabbar-height (60px) and .main pads with --space-md (16px) — AppShell.module.css:118-123. So on mobile the page box is computed 128px shorter than the viewport when it needs to be ~204px shorter, and the VirtualPosterGrid scroll area extends under the fixed tab bar. Not a grid-columns defect, so out of LD-14/LD-19 scope, but it is on the same page at the same breakpoint and a QA pass at 380px will see it.
